architecture.addressabilityLaw: An Agent that may change the current durable WorkingSet must be able to address the exact durable sources it is already seeing. Current cognition addressability is execution-control provenance, not additional task evidence.
architecture.sourceRangeLaw: WorkingSetViewProjector can mechanically compile each current exact HarnessWorkingSetPin together with the half-open request-message range [start,end) produced by that source. The mapping is derived from the current committed WorkingSet and exact HarnessWorkingViewSource objects.
architecture.requestProvenanceLaw: AgentTurnRequest may carry optional workingSetRefs containing each exact current pin and its request-message range. Existing serialized AgentTurnRequest values without workingSetRefs retain their legacy shape and remain readable.
architecture.providerVisibilityLaw: DeepSeek exposes current selected pin identities as workingSetSelection only when the WorkingSet-transition cognition surface is granted. Provider-message ranges are shifted by the Harness-authored system control message and disclosed as half-open [start,end) positions.
architecture.forgeryLaw: Continuity recomputes exact current WorkingSet pin/range provenance before Provider dispatch. A projector that supplies a forged pin identity while preserving the real message bytes is rejected with HarnessProviderCallRequestMismatch before the Adapter is invoked.
architecture.supersessionLaw: Durable correction is not a new Harness supersession action. The Agent first promotes exact corrected caller ingress when necessary, then uses the existing AgentWorkingSetTransitionProposal to retain the corrected/task pins and omit the stale pin.
architecture.semanticOwnershipLaw: Harness does not infer that newer text supersedes older text, does not compare contradictory claims semantically and does not decide which source should be dropped. The Agent owns the correction decision; Harness owns exact identity, provenance and lawful selection transition.
architecture.historyLaw: Omitting a stale pin removes it from current durable cognition but does not erase the source or earlier committed WorkingSet history. The stale exact pin remains inspectable/recallable through the existing historical cognition boundary.
architecture.progressLaw: P-C1.9 remains unchanged: reselecting identical pins is a lawful cognition-attempt reset but is not structural progress. The DeepSeek transition surface now states explicitly that same-pin transition is not a way to wait for caller input; needs_input remains the correct waiting conclusion.
architecture.privacyLaw: Exact current pin identities and ranges are disclosed to the model only on a transition-capable Provider surface and therefore require the Run's model-content authority. The system-control channel does not acquire Tool-content semantics merely because it carries identity metadata.
architecture.nonMemoryLaw: P-C1.12 adds no Memory CRUD API, semantic version graph, automatic contradiction resolver, tombstone system, relevance ranking, source summarizer or Harness-authored supersede operation.

behavior.exactRanges: A two-source WorkingSet with a one-message stale-code source and a two-message task source compiled to exact refs [0,1) and [1,3) bound to their exact pins. The model-visible WorkingView message order matched those ranges and Continuity Doctor remained healthy.
behavior.deepseekVisibility: A deterministic DeepSeek request with WorkingSet transitions enabled exposed workingSetSelection containing the exact stale pin and Provider-message range [1,2), accounting for the Harness system control message. The same AgentTurnRequest passed to an Adapter with WorkingSet transitions disabled did not disclose workingSetSelection.
behavior.forgedIdentity: A malicious projector returned the correct WorkingView bytes but substituted a forged resolvedDigest in the first current-source ref. Continuity rejected the Provider claim before Adapter invocation; the scripted Adapter observed zero requests and the durable store remained healthy.
behavior.deterministicCorrection: Starting from current durable [task, RED-9], a needs_input caller interaction supplied GREEN-42. The Agent promotion action produced current [task, RED-9, GREEN-42]. On the next turn the exact current refs allowed an ordinary WorkingSet transition to select only [task, GREEN-42]. RED-9 was absent from the final WorkingSet and final model view, while its exact pin remained present in the bounded committed WorkingSet history catalog.
behavior.legacyRequest: An AgentTurnRequest with no workingSetRefs serializes without the field and round-trips exactly, preserving historical request codec compatibility.

realModelExperiments.baselineCounterexample: Before current WorkingSet addressability existed, a correction experiment reached a state where GREEN-42 had been promoted alongside stale RED-9. The real model then explicitly reported that the exact logical ref/generation/slot/digest identities of the RED-9 and task sources were not visible, so it could not lawfully construct the requested transition without guessing. This falsified the idea that existing WorkingView content alone made ordinary transition sufficient for correction.
realModelExperiments.addressabilityRepair: After workingSetSelection was added, real-model requests contained exact current pins and their message provenance. The model no longer reported hidden identities and could quote exact current source identities from Harness execution control.
realModelExperiments.uncontrolledChurnObservation: In a broader uncontrolled correction probe, DeepSeek sometimes used lawful same-selection transitions while it should have waited for caller input or stopped after the selection was already corrected. P-C1.9 intentionally permits same-pin attempt reset, so P-C1.12 did not ban it; the transition Tool description was clarified that identical selection is an intentional attempt reset, not progress and not a substitute for needs_input.
realModelExperiments.finalControlledSupersession: In the final paired control, needs_input and exact GREEN-42 promotion were mechanically fixed so the only real-model decision was supersession from current [task, RED-9, GREEN-42]. Each of two independent DeepSeek probes used exactly one real Provider turn, read exact pins from workingSetSelection, proposed the existing WorkingSet transition retaining task plus corrected-code and omitting launch-code/RED-9, and produced current slots [corrected-code, task]. In both probes RED-9 was no longer current, GREEN-42 was current, the exact RED-9 pin remained in committed history, the Run stopped at the scripted next needs_input boundary, and Continuity Doctor was healthy.
realModelExperiments.finalWireLaw: The final real Provider wire offered propose_working_set_transition and submit_run_conclusion, included workingSetSelection, and required no new supersession control or Runtime Tool effect.

conclusion: P-C1.12 proves that the missing correction primitive was not semantic supersession but current-cognition addressability. Once the Agent can see exact current WorkingSet pin identities aligned to the exact model-message ranges they produced, existing P-C1.11 caller promotion plus existing P-C1.3 WorkingSet transition are sufficient to implement durable correction: promote GREEN-42, then select task + GREEN-42 and omit stale RED-9. Real deepseek-v4-flash probes performed that exact supersession in one Provider turn when the decision was isolated. The stale RED-9 source remains committed historical cognition rather than being erased. Harness still does not decide that GREEN-42 is truer or newer, and no Memory CRUD/supersede service, schema change or public API was required.
knownLimits: workingSetSelection makes exact identity addressable; it does not prove the semantic meaning, truth, freshness or authority of the source content.
P-C1.12 records no explicit semantic superseded_by edge or version graph. Supersession is represented structurally by later WorkingSet selection plus ordinary Journal chronology/basis.

The Agent may retain contradictory sources, drop the wrong source or repeatedly reset an attempt with identical pins. Harness validates lawful structure but does not become a semantic correction policy.

Current WorkingSet identity disclosure can include caller/domain-defined logical refs and generations. It is therefore exposed only on a model-authorized transition-capable Provider surface and may add prompt/token overhead for large WorkingSets.

The concrete WorkingSetViewProjector emits exact workingSetRefs. The request field remains optional for backward compatibility, so custom legacy projectors that do not implement range-aware projection may still omit current addressability and therefore retain the old Agent usability limitation.

Historical recall remains a separate explicitly granted cognition surface. Its Provider-faithful Tool-channel transcript still requires Tool-content authority even though current selection metadata itself uses the Harness system-control channel.

Caller correction must first become an exact materialized/selected source before ordinary transition can retain it after the caller interaction ends. P-C1.12 does not auto-materialize corrections independently of the P-C1.11 promotion law.

A same-selection transition remains lawful as an intentional attempt reset. The Provider description now explains that it is not progress or a waiting action, but Harness does not ban repeated lawful resets solely because a model uses them poorly.
No Runtime, World, Finance or Host repository was changed.
